data.turoyo: Aṯina bu darbo, kətwaylan ḥa kurmanǧ b qamuṯan, mhalaxwa, saliqina bi kaše, gnəḥtiwayna.
data.translation: Wir waren auf der Straße unterwegs, und vor uns fuhr ein Kurde her. Wir fuhren eine Steigung hinauf und schickten uns an, wieder hinabzufahren.

data.translation: Und wie es Gott fügte, als wir am Morgen aufbrachen und unseres Weges zogen, da war auch er mit seinem Pfluggespann beim Pflügen, entlang des Weges. Wir zogen an ihm vorüber und gingen auf gut Glück in ein anderes Dorf.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC Ishaq Material culture/98)

summary: example for sense 1 in Nomen Actionis (64/95)

data.turoyo: I naqqa d aṯi u šulṭono w u məǧləsayḏe, ḥəlle: kalayo ḥa rawixo ʕal ḥaṣe du səsyo, w d kətyo kačal, w kalayo ḥa mhalxono. U mhalxono, kəmmat, balki me gawa di bəḥto mofaqlux, ḥaqqaṣ d kətyo zʕuro layəq w šafiro.
data.translation: Als der Sultan und seine Ratsversammlung kamen, sah er: da sitzt einer auf dem Pferd, der ist kahlköpfig, und einer ist zu fuß. Der Fußgänger sieht aus, als ob du ihn aus dem Ei gepellt hättest, ein so hübscher und schmucker Bursche ist er.

summary: Routine counts supplied: II Preterit 267, Infectum 124, Imperativ 64, Nomen Actionis 10, Infectum-wa 8. These are additional summarized tokens and need no occurrence decisions.
Walking, riding and crawling are already combined in sense 1. L-series sole movers in the Preterit must remain in that box; semantic intransitivity alone does not create Preterit Intransitive.

Past ongoing or recurrent motion occurs in Infectum-wa; 26/132 is counterfactual obligation. Bare Infectum also supplies movement within past narration. Duration and repetition do not create separate senses.

mhalxono/mhalxone and halxo are BOTH already present, in two Nomen actionis sections. Reject reader claims that halxo or its box is wholly missing; retain the established filing as Nomen Actionis in added labels. 11/97, 71/47 and 75/14 already occur as example or note and are not repeated.
Contracted malax-, malx- forms occur across JTM, Ritter and MAC; retain source spelling. malaxxe can accompany an individual or a group, so no uniform person/number analysis is imposed.
68/24 combines b- manner and aʕmayna for the other party; 21/60 depicts a path outside advice, already quoted. Neither observation requires renumbering sense 1.
MAC NE Keze/14 omits the repeated walking sequence in English; 112/129 renders yawmo as Stunden. Neither is selected as a bilingual example.
Batch 2 preserves all batch-1 decisions and examples. New 1a concerns success of a matter and does not overturn the participant-extension treatment of customs and practices.
Motor travel now has a vehicle-subject example; the remaining repeated reduced Preterit proposals add no unrepresented form. 115/52 and 115/92 juxtapose reduced and full forms within one verse.
No secure new collocation is shown. halax (113/180) remains ambiguous between a bleached command and a particle; gəmhaxli (115/154) and -anne (115/92) remain source/morphology questions.
All 64 input records receive ordered occurrence decisions. Compact records have no supplied verses and are retained provisionally without new quotation.

Round 1 already has more than five ordinary Preterit and Infectum examples, six Infectum-wa examples, five Imperativ examples and both nominal shapes. Most reader thin-cell/new-form claims are therefore obsolete.

The Nomen Actionis material already includes halxo, mhalxono/mhalxone, human walkers, manner adjuncts and agreement-like predicates. New additions retain that label; no morphological boundary is silently changed.

Political halxo/halxe is repeatedly equated with miting and has a nominal event distribution. Finite halxo gədmhalxina links participation in the march to the specialised noun. The sentence is indexed once in each relevant form box, for its distinct nominal and finite tokens.
The three written haləx repetitions have only two supplied occurrence records; one quotation retains the whole source sequence, but no extra input decision is fabricated.

The corpus alternates full mhal- and reduced mal- forms. L-series Preterit movers, plural -na in Infectum, distance extents and habitual -wa remain separate morphological facts; there is no newly attested Detransitive.
Jan includes colloquial interview language and editorial prose. The structured-book navigation metaphor is a written-context extension; it is not enough to infer a separate lexical sense.
English is supplied machine translation. At Jan 1.46/1990 it renders walking/conduct as speaking, and at Jan 2.35/5549 it may omit negation. Neither problematic translation is quoted.
Do editors wish to distinguish agreement-bearing mhalxono/mhalxone from halxo within the two inherited Nomen Actionis sections? No new Infinitiv is established.
Is halux in 95/95, 112, 116, 118; 97/40; 98/18; 109/4 a verb variant of haləx or a presentative directive? These analyses remain provisional and no example is added.

Check mhalaxe (69/507), mhalaxla with a masculine traveller (70/30), Gəmhaxli/mhaxli/komhaxli (73/117, 294; 79/12), hat mhalxo (81/118), and mhalaxxena (98/9) against the editions or recordings; no spelling correction is invented.

summary: Motor, sea and airborne travel change the mode of movement, not the lexical meaning.

Abstract custom/practice as understood subject, conduct of a council, construction progress, moving plough and fixed architectural extent extend participants or path construal; they do not establish separate senses here.
Talay alternates driver, passengers and vehicle as sole participant of motor travel. m- can mark the village left behind; emigration is the discourse setting, not a new lexical meaning.
Jan independently supports the round-1 success/functioning subsense: orderly affairs, religious ordering and a question whether a matter can proceed.
Time moves on, evil walks before a person, and a reader finds a path inside a book. These change the participant or conceptual path; the evidence does not require separate numbered senses.
Biographical, moral and communal conduct follows a path or ancestral footsteps; it continues the inherited precept/advice uses.
